questions.stem: You share a lakehouse with a user who has no workspace role. They must query its tables through the SQL analytics endpoint and nothing more. What do you grant?

options.text: Build on the default semantic model only
The workspace Contributor role
Read plus Read all with SQL analytics endpoint
Read plus Read all with Apache Spark

questions.explanation: Sharing gives Read on the item. Adding Read all with SQL analytics endpoint lets the user query the tables through T-SQL; Read all with Apache Spark would also open the data to Spark.

questions.stem: A data scientist outside the workspace needs to read a lakehouse's files and tables from their own Spark notebooks. Which permission do you add when sharing the lakehouse?

options.text: Read all with SQL analytics endpoint
Read all with Apache Spark
Reshare
Build

questions.explanation: The Spark permission gives access to the lakehouse's data in OneLake, which Spark reads directly.

questions.stem: You share a warehouse with a user and grant no extra permissions. What can they do?

options.text: Connect to the warehouse, but read only objects they've been granted access to with T-SQL
Nothing; sharing without extra permissions fails
Edit every table
Read every table

questions.explanation: Read lets the user connect. Access to data then comes from the extra sharing permissions or from T-SQL GRANT statements on specific objects.

questions.stem: Which two statements about item-level sharing are true? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Shared items can't be read by groups
Sharing an item gives access to that item only, not to the rest of the workspace
Item sharing works only for reports
Item permissions can give someone less than any workspace role, such as only connecting to a shared warehouse
Sharing an item makes the user a workspace Viewer

questions.explanation: Item permissions apply to one item only. A plain share of a warehouse gives Read, which only lets the user connect, which is less than the Viewer role gives.

questions.stem: A workspace Contributor tries to share a warehouse with a business user, but sharing fails. What role must the person sharing have?

options.text: Any role, if the warehouse is endorsed
Contributor with Build permission
Admin or Member
Viewer

questions.explanation: Sharing a warehouse requires the Admin or Member workspace role.

questions.stem: You share a warehouse and select Read all data using SQL. What can the recipient do?

options.text: Read all tables and views in read-only mode, like the db_datareader role
Read the warehouse's files with Spark
Only connect, until you grant access with T-SQL
Read and write all tables

questions.explanation: Read all data using SQL grants ReadData, which reads all tables and views read-only and is the equivalent of db_datareader.

questions.stem: A support engineer must query DMVs such as sys.dm_exec_requests on a warehouse to troubleshoot slow queries, without reading business data. Which permission fits?

options.text: Monitor
ReadData
ReadAll
Audit

questions.explanation: Monitor lets a user query DMVs, query text, sessions and Insights views. Audit is for audit logs, and ReadData and ReadAll give access to data.

questions.stem: A user has Read all with SQL analytics endpoint on a shared lakehouse. They can query through the SQL endpoint URL but can't access the data through the lakehouse URL. What do you add?

options.text: Execute Apache Spark
SubscribeOneLakeEvents
Read all with Apache Spark
The Contributor workspace role

questions.explanation: Access through the lakehouse URL needs Read all with Apache Spark in addition to the SQL permission.

questions.stem: A partner team was given a shared lakehouse and now must write new files to it. What do you do?

options.text: Re-share the lakehouse with Read all with Apache Spark
Grant them a OneLake security role with read on the folder
Give them the Contributor role (or higher) on the workspace
Add the Reshare permission to the lakehouse

questions.explanation: Lakehouse sharing never gives write permissions, and OneLake security grants read only. Write access comes from a workspace role of Contributor or higher.

questions.stem: Which two statements about sharing a warehouse are true? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Recipients get access only to the shared warehouse, not to other items in the workspace
New or removed permissions can take up to two hours to propagate
You can share a warehouse directly with a service principal
Recipients can save their own queries in the warehouse editor
Recipients can reshare the warehouse with others

questions.explanation: Sharing is scoped to the one warehouse, and permission changes can take up to two hours. Recipients can't reshare, sharing with an SPN isn't supported, and shared recipients can't save queries.
